answer: Copper carries current in one direction only. Each ballot seals in copper — a hash of vote and key — pressed into shale before the beacon fires; then the beacon draws each ballot a vine, a random three-hop path it must climb in ninety seconds. A farm reusing one key dies by the shale check: two envelopes carrying one copper seal in one layer burn together, both stakes slashed. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 fresh seals at fifty minutes each — 8,333 hours — plus $35 staked per ballot, $350,000 frozen. A vine with two stems from one root is a weed the shale strangles.
